Bypoll results in Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam and Puducherry

Tamil Nadu: Vijay’s TVK expands its footprint

West Bengal: BJP’s march continues

Assam and Puducherry: Ruling parties hold ground

NEW DELHI: The ruling parties in the respective states continued to hold their ground as bypoll results were counted on Friday, October 9. In Tamil Nadu, it was still “Thalapathy” Vijay and his new but formidable TVK brigade making its presence felt. In West Bengal, the BJP’s commanding influence continued to open new doors, while in Assam, the saffron party remained firmly in the lead. Puducherry, meanwhile, stayed with the ruling side of chief minister N Rangaswamy.Tamil Nadu and West Bengal went to bypolls in two assembly constituencies each following their full-fledged assembly elections, which turned the political tide in both states and brought new ruling forces to power.Vijay’s TVK maintained comfortable leads in both Madurantakam and Dharapuram, seeking to expand its footprint in a state long dominated by Dravidian giants.TVK’s K Maragatham Kumaravel maintained a lead over DMK’s I Paranthamen in Madurantakam, while Sathyabama P was ahead of DMK’s Suganya in Dharapuram.Both constituencies had voted for the AIADMK in the previous Assembly elections, making TVK’s performance another sign of its growing electoral presence.The BJP, meanwhile, showed no signs of slowing down, maintaining huge leads in both Nandigram and Rejinagar.In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath was ahead of Congress’s Milan Pradhan in a constituency closely associated with chief minister Suvendu Adhikari’s political journey.Suvendu has won Nandigram in the last three consecutive assembly elections. In 2016, he was a close confidant of then-chief minister Mamata Banerjee. He later broke away from the TMC, joined the BJP and emerged as one of her fiercest political rivals.He has now succeeded former boss Mamata as chief minister of Bengal.In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar was also leading, keeping the contest competitive for the TMC candidate.The Bengal CM claimed that the BJP had secured around 60% of Muslim votes in Rejinagar and 80% in Nandigram, even as counting continued in both bypolls."Minority community found friend in BJP, voted for us in bypolls," Bengal CM Suvendu said after muslim-dominated Rejinagar supported the saffron party in big numbers.In Assam, the BJP appeared firmly placed in the contest for the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat, which fell vacant and went to a bypoll. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma was moving closer to victory as counting progressed.Puducherry, meanwhile, delivered a win for the ruling side, with chief minister N Rangaswamy’s party securing the Thattanchavady seat.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu and West Bengal went to bypolls in two assembly constituencies each following their full-fledged assembly elections. In Tamil Nadu, it was still “Thalapathy’ Vijay and his new but formidable TVK brigade making its presence felt. In West Bengal, the BJP’s commanding influence continued to open new doors. In Assam, the saffron party remained firmly in the lead. Puducherry stayed with the ruling side of chief minister N Rangaswamy.

Article Title: Mary Kom’s ex-husband alleges character assassination, files defamation complaint
Article Text:
Olympic medallist Mary Kom’s former husband, Karong Onkholer

Olympic medallist Mary Kom’s former husband, Karong Onkholer, has filed a defamation complaint against the boxer before Delhi’s Saket Court, alleging that remarks she made during a televised interview damaged his reputation.The complaint was filed on October 6 and is pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivam Gupta for pre-summoning evidence. The court is scheduled to hear the matter on November 19.According to the complaint, Onkholer and Kom married on March 12, 2005, and lived together in Faridabad. Their marriage was dissolved through customary practice on December 20, 2023, the complainant stated.Onkholer has alleged that Kom made defamatory remarks about him during a television interview aired on January 11, 2026, after the dissolution of their marriage. He claims the programme was broadcast to a nationwide audience running into millions.The complaint alleges that an ordinary viewer would interpret the statements, taken individually and collectively, as portraying Onkholer as “dishonest, unfaithful, unemployed, financially parasitic” and dependent on alcohol.It further alleges that the remarks suggested he had misappropriated money from Kom’s bank accounts and abandoned his responsibilities towards their children.The complainant has disputed the alleged portrayal of his professional life, stating that he sacrificed his own career and professional pursuits to support Kom’s boxing career before and during their marriage. The complaint says this account contradicts the alleged assertion that he had no career and had never been gainfully employed.Describing Kom as an internationally renowned boxing champion with a substantial public following, the complaint argues that the broadcast carried the potential to harm his standing as a spouse and parent.Onkholer has approached the court through advocates Akash Krishna and Pragati Sharma. The complaint invokes Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with defamation.The allegations are part of a pending complaint and have not been established in court. The next hearing on November 19 is expected to determine the subsequent course of the proceedings as the court considers the matter at the pre-summoning evidence stage.
Article Summary: Olympic medallist Mary Kom’s former husband, Karong Onkholer, has filed a defamation complaint against the boxer. The complaint was filed on October 6 and is pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivam Gupta for pre-summoning evidence. The court is scheduled to hear the matter on November 19.

Article Title: 'Women police personnel molested': Centre's charge puts Rahul Gandhi-led protest in focus
Article Text:
Centre flags alleged incidents amid Rahul Gandhi row

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Friday defended the security measures and restrictions imposed in Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s planned protest on October 10, telling the Supreme Court that the steps were necessary to ensure the safety of residents.However, the court expressed concern over the disruption to public transport, cautioning authorities against going overboard in the name of security.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, argued that law enforcement agencies had to take preventive measures in view of the planned demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Referring to recent protests in the national capital, Centre alleged that "women police personnel had been molested, attacked and injured," over the last few days.The submission brought Congress leader Rahul Gandhi into the spotlight once again, after the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party accused the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha of behaving “inappropriately” with a woman police officer during a protest a day earlier.BJP leader Kesavan had criticised Rahul over the alleged incident, asking, “How can any decent individual, let alone a member of parliament or a leader of the opposition, behave in such an inappropriate manner with a woman, and that too, a female police personnel?”However, the top court questioned the extent of the restrictions imposed in the capital, particularly the proposed closure of Metro stations and disruption to railway services ahead of Saturday’s protest.“Exercise caution, there's nothing wrong with that. Police are responsible for maintaining law and order,” the court observed on the security arrangements for the October 10 demonstration.Taking up the issue of Metro station closures, the court cautioned that security measures should not bring daily life to a standstill.“Law enforcement agencies can't bring everything to halt & leave people without any transport facility,” it said.The court also questioned whether the restrictions were proportionate to the threat, remarking, “One should not use hammer to kill fly,” while referring to the closure of Delhi Metro stations ahead of the CJP protest.The hearing came amid heightened security across the national capital, with authorities stepping up arrangements and imposing restrictions in wake of the October 10 protest demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.
Article Summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court that the steps were necessary to ensure the safety of residents. The court expressed concern over the disruption to public transport, cautioning authorities against going overboard in the name of security. The hearing came amid heightened security across the national capital, with authorities stepping up arrangements.

Article Title: 'Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai': Delhi Police issues 'open letter' to protesters

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has issued an open letter to citizens, emphasising that protecting their safety is its responsibility and that police personnel, despite wearing uniforms, are human beings with families and loved ones."Dear citizen, Aapki awaaz aapka haq hai, aur aapki surakhsha hamara farz. Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai, jiska aapna Parivar hai, apne log hai. Farq sirf uniform ka hai, insaaniyat ka nahi," the letter read.(Your voice is your right, and your safety is our duty. Behind the uniform is also a human being, who has a family and loved ones. The only difference is the uniform, not humanity).The open letter comes amid heightened tensions over protests in the national capital after the Delhi Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10. The police cited the late submission of its application, non-compliance with rules during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order, and traffic management.Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the New Delhi district police received an application from CJP co-convenor Saurabh Das on October 7, seeking permission to hold a protest demanding accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“On October 7, 2026, an application from Saurabh Das, Co-Convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party, was received in the New Delhi District. As per the application, an intimation was given regarding a protest to be held at Jantar Mantar on October 10 concerning the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). Upon processing this intimation, it was found that the notice was received at very short notice. Under current guidelines, an application to organise an event at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the scheduled date,” Prasad said.Meanwhile, Delhi Police on Monday issued an advisory for journalists covering protests, asking them to carry valid identity cards issued by their respective organisations or PIB/DIP accreditation cards and keep them visibly displayed to facilitate identification by law enforcement personnel.The advisory urged media personnel to ensure their presence and activities did not obstruct police operations or the movement of security personnel. Journalists were also advised to maintain a reasonable and safe distance while covering and recording proceedings during tense situations.They were further asked to position themselves in a manner that clearly distinguished them from protesters, particularly at crowded sites where police personnel are deployed. The police said the measures were intended to facilitate the identification of journalists and prevent interference with police operations.
Article Summary: The open letter comes amid heightened tensions over protests in the national capital. The Delhi Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10. The police cited the late submission of its application, non-compliance with rules during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety.

Article Title: Deeply Offensive: Government rebuts Vance’s indentured servants remark
Article Text:
The ministry also cautioned in its response that the steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Following a long period of strained India-US ties, the gloves came off finally as India hit out at US Vice President JD Vance for labelling H-1B visa holders and foreign tech professionals as foreign indentured servants - a characterisation New Delhi slammed as deeply offensive and unwarranted.The scathing response followed the US announcement about the suspension of many tech companies, including several from India, from the PERM Green Card programme. Vance had reinforced the announcement by declaring that American workers cannot be laid off and then replaced with foreign indentured servants. He also insisted that only top-tier, elite foreign talent that's not available domestically should be brought in.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) countered Vance's comments as it said in a formal statement that such descriptions were unwarranted and ignored the fact that Indian professionals in the US are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem."Indeed, the history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity.Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," said the ministry, adding it will continue to follow developments related to the issue.The unusually blunt pushback suggests India's patience is wearing thin after a series of bilateral setbacks, ranging from trade and tariffs, immigration and talent mobility to India's ties with Russia and Washington's Pakistan outreach. External affairs minister S Jaishankar had recently warned that the US' growing ties with Pakistan would hurt the India-US relationship.The ministry also cautioned in its response that the steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries. It said talent mobility adds value to both economies, creating opportunities for Indians and helping US companies equally with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US."This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact," said the Indian government.However, the statement also took note of the fact that PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme. "The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies," said the ministry.While the America First signalling through the announcement seems designed for an electoral boost in the upcoming mid-term polls, it's unlikely to help the already rocky state of India-US ties. The timing is also problematic as it creates poor optics for PM Narendra Modi's visit to the US in December for the G20 summit. It also comes just ahead of Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India this month, during which India will look to raise its concerns related to the issue.The US announcement is the latest flashpoint in ties after the US Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA), a new law that empowers the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries importing Russian oil. Modi had raised India's anxieties about that issue in a phone call with President Donald Trump late last month.
Article Summary: India hit out at US Vice President JD Vance for labelling H-1B visa holders and foreign tech professionals as foreign indentured servants. New Delhi slammed characterisation as deeply offensive and unwarranted. The scathing response followed the US announcement about the suspension of many tech companies, including several from India.

Article Title: Patrón co-founder John Paul DeJoria turned a 96-acre Texas ranch into a home for more than 120 exotic animals; when it sold for $6.93 million, the buyer inherited the herd and a 2,700-square-foot unde
Article Text:
The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin.

A ranch that came with more than a house

The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms.

The underground shelter

The animals were part of the deal

Why DeJoria sold the ranch

DeJoria co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989.

A 96-acre Texas ranch once owned by Patrón Tequila co-founder John Paul DeJoria came with an unusual combination of luxury, wildlife and an underground shelter. More than 120 exotic African animals lived on the property, while the estate also had a 7,540-square-foot main house, two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin, and stretched along 2,600 feet of Fitzhugh Creek. According to the Houston Chronicle, the property was listed for $7.495 million in 2016 after initially being put on the market for $7.99 million. It eventually sold for $6.93 million. As reported by ABC13 Houston, television director Jonathan Nowzaradan is the buyer of the ranch.The property was not simply a large Texas home. Its listing described it as an exotic-animal ranch, and the buyer was set to inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. According to the Houston Chronicle, the animals were part of the property when it was listed. The ranch included two barns, each with attached guest quarters, along with a stocked pond and a pecan orchard. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the animals included more than 120 exotic species and that the property was being sold with the animals and its furnishings.The estate itself covered 96 acres and overlooked Fitzhugh Creek, which feeds from Barton Creek. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. It featured wood-beamed ceilings, hardwood floors, partial stone walls and a large gourmet kitchen with a commercial-grade stove. Outside, there was a pool and spa, an outdoor kitchen and a wide porch overlooking the surrounding Hill Country.One of the property's more unusual features was underground. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the ranch included a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The Austin Business Journal also described the property as having a “2,700-square underground shelter.” So, when the ranch changed hands, the buyer was getting far more than a luxury residence. The property came with its land, buildings, underground shelter and a large collection of exotic animals.The exotic animals were among the details that made the ranch unusual in the first place. As reported by The Houston Chronicle, the new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. The ranch was a 96-acre property with a spa pool, limestone walls and the animals. The animals included species such as gazelles, wildebeest and antelopes.DeJoria, best known for co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems and Patrón Spirits Company, had owned Patrón de Paz since 2008, as reported by the San Antonio Express-News. Realtor Dave Murray said DeJoria's primary residence was near Lake Austin and that he had decided to sell the Dripping Springs ranch. Murray also said DeJoria owned several other homes around the world and was selling four estates at the time. DeJoria co-founded John Paul Mitchell Systems with hairdresser Paul Mitchell in 1980 and later co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989. The ranch's sale meant that its next owner did not simply acquire a large piece of Texas Hill Country property. The $6.93 million deal also brought with it a ready-made exotic-animal ranch, two barns, a creekside estate, a stocked pond and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter.
Article Summary: The ranch, known as ‘Patrón de Paz,’ was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. The ranch included two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals.

Article Title: 'Complete stoppage of metro, rail services unacceptable': SC to Centre ahead of CJP October 10 Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:
SC says restrictions cannot be reconsidered unless denial of permission for CJP protest is challenged.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday raised concerns over the closure of Metro station entry gates ahead of the October 10 CJP protest in Delhi, saying the restrictions would affect thousands of commuters.The court pointed out that students, employees and senior citizens travelling from Gurugram, Greater Noida and other parts of Delhi-NCR would be among those affected."Everybody does not have a car… You cannot bring everything to a halt and leave people without any transport facility," Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said.The apex court also asked the Centre to ensure that train services to Delhi and metro operations are not completely suspended ahead of the October 10 protest."We make it clear that there shall be no complete prohibition on movement of metro trains," Supreme Court said.SC said services should continue in a regulated manner to minimise inconvenience to the public.The observations came as a team of senior advocates led by Kapil Sibal moved the Supreme Court against the cancellation of trains and proposed closure of Metro stations ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's ( CJP ) protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.During an earlier hearing, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant had questioned why the protesters had not challenged Delhi Police's decision to deny permission for the demonstration at Jantar Mantar.The court observed that it could not consider easing the restrictions unless the denial of permission was challenged."If there is no permission for protests, it will be an unlawful protest," Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed.Sibal, appearing for CPM MP M A Baby, argued that every citizen had the right to protest, even spontaneously.The Supreme Court said the right to peaceful protest at a designated place existed, but holding a demonstration without permission could expose protesters to prosecution.The bench also indicated that it could consider easing the restrictions if the organisers challenged the denial of permission and gave assurances about the gathering.The court said it could seek details about the number of people expected to attend, along with undertakings that protesters would remain peaceful and not carry weapons.Such assurances could allow the court to reconsider restrictions imposed over possible law and order concerns.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Delhi Police's decision to deny permission for the protest.He argued that Jantar Mantar was a designated protest site and police permission was not required to hold a demonstration there.Dipke also criticised the Centre over the cancellation of trains to Delhi ahead of Saturday's protest."Shut down entire country if you are scared of youth," he said, taking aim at the government over the restrictions.Delhi Police had earlier denied permission for the proposed protest, citing short notice, alleged violations during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order and traffic management.Joint commissioner of police Nupur Prasad said the police had received an application from CJP co-convener Saurav Das seeking permission for a protest over the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner."This intimation was considered, and it was found that the intimation was given in a very short span of time, whereas as per the prescribed guideline, the intimation has to be received 10 days prior to the protest that is planned," she said.Prasad also pointed to the party's conduct during an earlier protest at the same venue."Further, it is also important to mention that on an earlier occasion, when the Cockroach Janta Party was given permission to hold a protest there, they did not follow the lawful directions and did not follow their own undertakings given at that point in time," she said.She added that Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which allows preventive restrictions to maintain public order, was in force in the New Delhi area.Police warned that anyone violating the restrictions could face legal action.The restrictions come ahead of Saturday's planned CJP protest, with several trains to New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin cancelled and restrictions proposed at Metro stations.
Article Summary: SC says restrictions cannot be reconsidered unless denial of permission for CJP protest is challenged. Delhi Police had earlier denied permission for the proposed protest. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Delhi Police's decision to deny permission.

Article Title: 'Unwarranted, offensive': India slams US Vice President JD Vance 'indentured servants' amid H-1B visa row

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday slammed US vice-president JD Vance over his description of H-1B visa workers as "indentured servants", calling his remarks "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive".In a statement, responding to Vance’s comments, the ministry said, "We have also seen some comments in this context by the US Vice President. We believe that such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem."The MEA also highlighted the contribution of immigrants to the US economy, saying, "Indeed, the history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity.""Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," it added.Vance made the remarks while addressing a news conference on visa fraud, alleging that companies bring in foreign workers at lower wages while laying off American employees.“If you are working as an H-1B visa in the United States of America, you’re earning $20,000 less than an American citizen hired in the same position.If you were brought in by one of these foreign outsourcing firms, you’re making $48,000 less than an American citizen in a similar position," Vance said."So, I’m sure that everybody here understands the game that is being played. You bring in indentured servants from outside the country, you lay off American workers and, if you’re a corporation, you make a ton of money by under cutting the wages of American workers, replacing them with people who frankly shouldn’t be in the United States of America to begin with,” he added.The MEA said that it was aware of the US department of labor’s decision concerning the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies."It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US," the statement said."This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries,” it added.The MEA also clarified that PERM is separate from the H-1B visa programme. It said the suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents, although it could affect the green card process for eligible employees of the companies concerned.“We continue to follow developments around this issue,” the ministry added.The MEA’s response came a day after the Trump administration suspended eight companies, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from participating in the PERM programme.The US administration’s move is part of a broader crackdown on skilled-worker immigration. US officials have alleged that companies have used the system at the expense of American workers.The US department of labor said it would stop accepting and processing new and pending PERM applications involving the affected companies.PERM is an important step in the employment-based green card process. Employers generally need labour certification from the US department of labor before sponsoring eligible foreign workers for permanent residence.The process requires employers to establish that there are not enough qualified, willing and available US workers for a position and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect wages and working conditions.
Article Summary: US vice-president JD Vance described workers coming in on H1B visas as 'indentured servants' The ministry of external affairs called his remarks "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive" Vance made the remarks while addressing a news conference on visa fraud.

Article Title: Plane hit, pilot killed: Riyadh airport attacks by Houthi kill three, damages Saudia aircraft

Three Saudi nationals were killed and several others injured in two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a Saudia Airlines aircraft on Thursday, Saudi Arabia’s general authority of civil aviation said on Friday.The first attack targeted airport facilities, while the second struck the aircraft, the authority said. It did not identify those responsible, although Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen claimed to have targeted the airport, as cited by AP.Saudia Airlines has confirmed that a pilot was killed and an aircraft was damaged in the attack.Operations at King Khalid International Airport have since resumed, with air traffic returning to normal, according to the civil aviation authority.The attacks come amid a heightened security situation in Saudi Arabia following separate strikes on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport on October 6 and 7. Those attacks left three people dead and 36 injured, according to the authority. Two people were killed and 28 injured at Abha airport, while one person was killed and eight injured at King Khalid International Airport.Saudi Civil Defence personnel responded to Thursday’s incident after a missile was launched by the Houthi militia, the Saudi Civil Defence said.Following the attacks on civilian facilities, Saudi-led coalition forces said they had destroyed 82 military targets belonging to the Houthi militia in Yemen.Amid the security situation, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh on Thursday advised Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain vigilant, stay indoors when necessary and follow instructions issued by local authorities through official channels.“In view of the current situation, all Indian nationals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia are advised to remain alert and vigilant, stay indoors as necessary, and follow the instructions issued by local authorities through official channels. Indian nationals are strongly advised to refrain from circulating or reposting any videos or news related to the ongoing events," the embassy said in an advisory.The mission said the Embassy of India in Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah, including their outsourced services through VFS, continued to operate normally and would issue further updates as required."The Embassy of India, Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah and its outsourced services through VFS, are continuing to function normally and will issue updates and advisories as and when necessary. The 24x7 helpline of Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra (PBSK) remains available on Toll free No: 8002471234,” it added.India on Thursday condemned the attacks on the two Saudi airports, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure “completely unacceptable”.In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs said, “India condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.”“The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable,” the MEA said, expressing condolences to the families of those killed and wishing those injured a speedy recovery.

Article Title: ‘Lot of talk about one company’: Centre tells satcom firms to meet security norms amid Musk's Starlink row

NEW DELHI: Communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia on Friday said satellite communication (satcom) companies can begin operations in India only after individually meeting the required security conditions and milestones, stressing that three companies have received licences despite the focus on Elon Musk ’s Starlink. He also took a dig at Congress for their response to Musk's statements.“There is a lot of conversation about one specific company, but three companies have got satcom licences,” Scindia said, underlining that each operator must fulfil the required conditions before it can start services.Scindia’s remarks come amid a row between Musk and the Indian government over the delay in Starlink’s commercial launch in the country. The government called suggestions of discriminatory treatment “baseless and misconceived”.Minister of state for communications Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani said the security clearance issue was pending with the ministry of home affairs and had “nothing to do with one company”.Scindia also took a swipe at Congress saying that the party had earlier objected to a particular person getting a licence but was now aligned with the same person in questioning why the licence had not been granted. He accused the party of not knowing whether it was “going left or right”.The remarks come after Musk stepped up his criticism on Thursday, saying Starlink was licensed in more than 165 countries and had spent five years complying with Indian government requirements. He questioned why the company was still awaiting approval and asked whether industrialist Mukesh Ambani was the “real boss of India”.Leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi responded to Musk on X, writing: “Welcome to India, Elon. Article Title: INDIA bloc protests against CEC: 'Unite to fight' proposes Uddhav's Sena; will AAP, DMK relent?
Article Text:
Both AAP and DMK have exited the INDIA bloc.

-

'A very critical request'

Will DMK, AAP join SIR protests?

'All parties should look at larger picture'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Should Arvind Kejriwal ’s AAP and MK Stalin ’s DMK join INDIA bloc’s fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over SIR? Well, the answer would surely be “yes”, as far as the allies of the bloc are concerned.Now to the more difficult question: Will Arvind Kejriwal’s AAP and MK Stalin’s DMK join INDIA bloc’s fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over SIR? Well, there is no straight answer to this one.The AAP and the DMK have a common enemy in the Congress . Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena (UBT) has now urged the two parties to set aside their differences with the grand-old-party to fight against "dictatorship". In an editorial in the party mouthpiece 'Saamana', Shiv Sena (UBT) said, “The entire country has been witnessing protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), but the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) have stayed away from it."The absence of both parties, who have officially withdrawn from the INDIA bloc, has highlighted the existing differences within the opposition camp on the strategy and format of the protest against irregularities in the SIR process.Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha feels Shiv Sena (UBT)'s suggestion to both the DMK and the Aam Aadmi Party to join the INDIA bloc is a very practical, very reasonable, and at the moment, a very critical request."This is not about, at the moment, anything other than the fact that Indian democracy is in peril. It is unlikely that the CEC is going to resign of his own volition. It is pretty apparent that the government of Mr. Modi is going to be stubborn, and they will stonewall any effort by the opposition to demand and get accountability. Public protests don't seem to make any difference to the government. So the more the merrier," Sanjay Jha says.While the AAP has openly announced it will not be a part of the INDIA bloc’s protest and said “we are fighting this battle in our own way, the DMK has spoken in different tones.DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai accused Rahul of adopting inconsistent positions on the electoral roll revision exercise and questioned why developments in Tamil Nadu had not received the same attention as the broader campaign against the Election Commission.In a post on X, Annadurai called on Rahul Gandhi to clarify his stand on allegations concerning names allegedly removed from Tamil Nadu’s electoral rolls during the SIR process.The DMK spokesperson also referred to a statement attributed to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge that governments elected after the SIR exercise should be dissolved and sought clarification on why Rahul Gandhi had not publicly endorsed that position and whether such a stand would also apply to Tamil Nadu.Interestingly, a day later, DMK senior leader TKS Elangovan backed Rahul Gandhi on protests against the Election Commission (EC), saying that citizens have a right to protest against the government.“It is the right of citizens to fight against the government’s wrongdoings. That is what Rahul Gandhi did yesterday. Still, this government does not want him to protest because Gyanesh Kumar is being very useful to the BJP. Because of him, the BJP captured power in many states. In all these states, re-elections should be held,” Elangovan said.The DMK and the Congress had a very unpleasant parting of their two-decade-old ties after the 2026 assembly elections in Tamil Nadu, which the alliance lost to actor-politician C Joseph Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK. While the TVK emerged as the single largest party, it fell short of a majority. The Congress rushed in to help Vijay not just form the government but also eventually join it. Making Congress a part of the government was something the DMK had resisted all along. The Congress move offended the DMK to no end. Since then, MK Stalin’s party has been unrelenting in its attacks on the Congress at all forums from Chennai to Delhi. The Congress, on its part, maintains that it kept the DMK in the loop while shifting loyalties to the TVK.The DMK is missing no opportunity to drive a wedge between the new allies. On Thursday, it lashed out at Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay-led TVK for not explicitly naming the BJP government over the arrest of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi after a protest in the national capital demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Questioning the TVK's statement, Elangovan pointed out that it failed to identify the authorities responsible for the action against the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha. "Who arrested Rahul Gandhi? They should condemn and explicitly mention the name of the BJP government," Elangovan told PTI videos.With the TVK establishing itself as the third pole of Tamil Nadu politics, at least for now, the Congress will have to choose one against the other, and to that extent its ties with the DMK will remain frosty for now. More so, after the TVK has officially joined the INDIA bloc. But the DMK’s measured criticism of the Congress-led INDIA bloc protests may offer a ray of hope to the opposition bloc allies of a future softening of stand by M K Stalin.Now, let’s turn to AAP. Here’s where untangling the strains in the ties may be very difficult, if not impossible. Relations between the Congress and the AAP have always been uneasy and tumultuous. AAP was initially a part of the INDIA bloc.However, ties between Kejriwal’s party and the Congress were never smooth given their competing political interests in several states. AAP attended the first three meetings of the INDIA bloc. The high point in their ties came in the run up to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections when the two parties agreed to a joint contest in Delhi, Haryana, Goa, Punjab and Gujarat.The alliance did not work and the ties ended for all practical purposes after the results were out. In July 2025, Kejriwal formally announced the end of ties.Uddhav Thackeray’s party has reminded Kejriwal of his bitter experiences with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and the Election Commission.“While Kejriwal was the chief minister of Delhi, he was put behind bars in a "false" case. Kejriwal's defeat was engineered by deleting names of voters from his constituency, it alleged. So, it is not in the AAP's interest to stay away from the INDIA bloc,” the Shiv Sena (UBT) wrote in its editorial.Sanjay Jha is confident that these parties will eventually join the opposition protest. He argues it is extremely crucial that the opposition includes everyone.“Whether there are any small, petty differences, whether there is any degree of discomfort with one or the other partner, everyone has to look at the larger picture. And the larger picture is that today people are out on the streets because they're concerned about the future of their vote and the future of democracy,” Sanjay Jha says.“And I believe it is very likely that the DMK and Arvind Kejriwal will join, because this is the time to put aside any petty squabbles and think of the larger goal of the country,” he adds.But this may be easier said than done. The Congress and the AAP are the main rivals in Punjab, where assembly elections are due early next year. The two parties are already engaged in a bitter war of words in Punjab, where AAP is defending its only government and the Congress is going all out to defeat Kejriwal’s party and reclaim its lost glory and government in the state.So, let’s see if this political compulsion decides the future course of ties between the two parties or the “larger goal of the country”?
Article Summary: Both AAP and DMK have exited the INDIA bloc. Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena (UBT) has urged the two parties to set aside their differences with the grand-old- party to fight against "dictatorship"

Article Title: 'Jantar Mantar a designated site to protest, police permission not needed': Abhijeet Dipke on October 10 stir
Article Text:
CJP founder slams Centre over train cancellations

Dipke invokes Article 19

NEW DELHI: A day ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest in Delhi, its founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday hit out at the authorities over restrictions on public transport, saying the government should shut down the entire country if it was scared of the youth.The CJP has called for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, alleging large-scale irregularities in the Election Commission’s special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Railway Board on Friday cancelled certain mail and express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on October 10. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police urged the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to shut 57 metro stations to prevent the movement of youths expected to join the protest.Speaking to reporters, Dipke questioned the restrictions and maintained that government permission was not required to protest at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site.Questioning the measures taken ahead of the demonstration, Dipke said, "What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down metro, what should one do?""Shut down the entire country if you are scared of the youth," he said.The Delhi Police, however, denied permission for the CJP’s proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, citing short notice, past non-compliance with directions and concerns over public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation.Dipke also questioned the inconvenience caused to commuters, arguing that restrictions on public transport and roads would themselves create difficulties for ordinary people."Is Delhi a property of Narendra Modi or Amit Shah? Is this their ancestral property? Is this their paternal property? On one hand, you say that due to the protest, people are facing inconvenience, and on the other hand, you shut down all the metro, you shut down all the railways, you block all the roads. Now, won't there be inconvenience for people?" he said.Dipke said CJP activists were prepared to face detention or arrest over the planned demonstration."How many people will they detain? Arrest me, detain me! Saurabh is ready, Ashutosh is ready. Arrest me, detain me!" he said.Questioning the need for police permission, Dipke invoked Article 19 of the Constitution, which guarantees certain freedoms, including the right to assemble peacefully, subject to constitutional restrictions. He argued that Jantar Mantar was a designated site for protests."Did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? Before deleting 13 crore votes, did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? The Supreme Court didn't even give approval for the Form 6 modification. So, when Gyanesh Kumar, without telling anyone, without asking anyone, deletes 13 crore votes, then to protest against him, the constitutional right we have according to Article 19, what is the need for permission?" he said.Dipke also questioned the Delhi Police’s requirement that applications to hold protests at Jantar Mantar be submitted at least 10 days in advance, linking the rule to the restrictions imposed ahead of Saturday’s planned demonstration.The CJP’s proposed protest centres on its allegations of irregularities in the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke hits out at authorities over restrictions on public transport. CJP has called for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. What are the major concerns

NEW DELHI: SpaceX CEO and the world's richest man Elon Musk on Thursday went on a rant explaining how the Starlink's satellite internet services will help the "least served" in India. Musk had just a day earlier alleged that his telecom firm was facing regulatory hurdles in India due to "oligarchs", a claim which was strongly rejected by the Indian government.The SpaceX chief then launched a tweet blitz posting about thrice in just a span of 10 minutes."Starlink will help the least-served in India," he said in a post at 6:18pm.He followed it up with another post at 6:25pm, writing, "Starlink provides Internet connectivity to the least-served, enabling self-education and prosperity by giving people access to sell their products worldwide!"Three minutes later, Elon posted again: "People who oppose @Starlink hurt only the least-served. The wealthy or those living in large cities already have good Internet, so they don’t understand."Musk's comments come as a Starlink delegation is attending the India Mobile Congress organised in the national captial.Musk's claim about Starlink serving the "least-served" in India is somewhat ironic, as India already ranks among the countries with the lowest internet charges in the world."The last decade was about scalability, penetration, affordability.We have discussed many times of how voice prices have crashed, data prices have lowered by almost 97%, which has led to greater penetration," information & technology minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said on Thursday.On the other hand, Starlink will reportedly cost Rs 8,600 per month, with an additional Rs 34,000 one-time hardware charge."Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are … This is a crime against the people of India!" Musk said in a post on Wednesday.The telecom ministry rejected Musk's claim stating, "Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all three licensees""The Department of Telecom has issued licences to all satcom companies as well as provisional spectrum. Now the issue is pending with MHA for security clearance. As soon as it is cleared, they will get it. It has nothing to do with one company," minister of state for communications Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani told reporters on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress.READ ALSO: 'Remain alert, stay indoors': India issues advisory for citizens in Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks The logic behind Starlink is simple: Get internet to places where conventional networks are difficult or too expensive to reach. But Elon Musk’s satellite internet service has increasingly become much more than a tool for connectivity. Its growing use in war zones, conflict areas and during internet shutdowns has turned Starlink into a strategic technology and raised questions over who controls access to it.Critics have raised concerns about the company’s links with US intelligence and military agencies, arguing that a privately controlled satellite network could have implications for national security and sovereignty.Starlink uses thousands of small satellites in low-Earth orbit, around 550km above the planet. Unlike traditional communications satellites positioned around 36,000km away, these satellites can transmit data with lower latency. Users connect through a small receiver with an electronically controlled antenna, which automatically links with satellites passing overhead. The satellites can also transfer data between themselves using laser links.A 2024 report by the Kutniti Foundation, had described Starlink as “a wolf in sheep’s clothing”. The foundation argued that Starlink’s global satellite network gives it capabilities that go beyond conventional telecom services and could create strategic concerns for countries such as India.Furthermore, the satellites also raise security questions. Satellites travel at roughly 11,000 km/h to 28,000 km/h orbiting the earth and can also be used to monitor activity inside the territory of a country.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO and the world's richest man Elon Musk on Thursday went on a rant explaining how the Starlink's satellite internet services will help the "least served" in India. Musk had just a day earlier alleged that his telecom firm was facing regulatory hurdles in India due to "oligarchs", a claim which was strongly rejected by the Indian government. Critics have raised concerns about the company's links with US intelligence and military agencies.

NEW DELHI: “Mask must face the same consequences as the Face”, “If your masters are in jail, you will serve them better by being there, not outside” – were the caustic remarks by Supreme Court on Thursday as it send back to prison an accused who was granted bail by the Punjab and Haryana HC in a huge narcotic drug trafficking case.The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar and subsequent unearthing of an inter-state illegal drug trafficking syndicate. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on the liberty of citizens and because of his illegal custody.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked, given the gravity of the crime, a Rs 3,000 crore illegal drug trafficking syndicate and seizure of 5,000 Tramadol tablets, can the illegal detention prior to arrest vitiate the arrest itself as has been cited by the HC?When Singh said that his client, Anuj Kumar Singh, was a mere employee of those who were allegedly running the inter-state drug trafficking network, the bench said, “You are a ‘mukhota’ (mask) which was as much involved in the crime as the face itself.”“When your masters are in jail, you can serve them better by being there with them, not outside,” the bench said while expressing serious concern over the menace of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in the state. The senior advocate said that there was no evidence of any seizure of drugs from his client.The bench said, “In a game of football, there are 11 players but all of them do not have possession of the ball simultaneously.”The counsel said his client was not even a 12th player. Switching to cricket from football, the bench said, “He was either a cover or an extra-cover.”The bench said it would cancel the bail, ask the prosecution to complete the trial in one year and if it does not complete, then the accused can apply for regular bail. When Singh protested saying the accused had cooperated with the investigation and regularly attended trial while being on bail, the bench said, “For a Rs 3,000 crore drug trafficking case, one year in jail is nothing.”It asked the accused to surrender within two weeks and asked him to respond to the Union govt’s appeal against HC order granting bail.When Singh cited the HC’s decision to grant bail because of illegal custody prior to arrest and the premium it put on liberty, the bench said, “We also continuously ruled in favour of preserving liberty if there are other redeeming features. In your case, we do not find your cooperation in investigation or attendance of trial in the face of nature of crime and the restrictions in law to be a very relevant redeeming feature. Your arguments are most persuasive. In any other case we would have agreed with you.”
Article Summary: The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on liberty of citizens.

Article Title: 'PERM distinct from H-1B visa': MEA on US move to suspend certain firms from green card programme
Article Text:
File photo: MEA says US move against tech firms may affect green card process, not H-1B status

Which companies have been suspended?

What is PERM, and how is it different from H-1B?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the US government's decision to suspend several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme would not, by itself, affect existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents.The ministry said the suspension of applications under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme could, however, affect the permanent residency process for eligible employees of the companies concerned.“We are aware of the US Department of Labour’s decision concerning the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies. It should be noted that PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme,” the MEA said in a statement.“The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies,” it added.The ministry also emphasised the economic benefits of skilled talent moving between India and the US, saying the latest measures did not advance the shared ambitions of the two countries.“It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US,” the MEA said.“This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries,” it added.The US department of labour has suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini from the PERM programme. The department said it would not accept new applications from the affected companies or process their pending applications amid multiple active federal investigations.US labour secretary Keith Sonderling said the companies had collectively sought millions of foreign workers and received hundreds of thousands of approvals under employment-based immigration programmes.“Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications. That's hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers,” Sonderling said.The administration has alleged that companies misused employment-based immigration programmes to replace American workers with foreign employees. These are allegations made by US officials; the announcement cited ongoing investigations.PERM is a labour-certification process that allows an eligible US employer to sponsor a foreign worker for employment-based permanent residency, commonly known as a green card. Before certifying an application, the US department of labour must establish that there are not enough qualified and available American workers for the job and that employing the foreign worker would not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed US workers.The H-1B programme, by contrast, allows US employers to hire skilled foreign workers temporarily for specialised occupations. The PERM suspension does not automatically cancel existing H-1B visas, but it could disrupt a route to permanent residency for employees whose employers are sponsoring them through the programme.The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. A day before the announcement, the US department of homeland security proposed new fees for F-1 international students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), describing the measure as an effort to protect American workers and strengthen the integrity of the immigration system.
Article Summary: The US government has suspended several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme. The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini have been suspended.

Article Title: Environment protection versus strategic infrastructure: SC seeks Punjab plan on afforestation
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In what appeared to be a clash between environment protection and strategic infrastructure in a border state, the Supreme Court on Thursday asked Punjab govt its plan on allocation of land for compensatory afforestation in lieu of tree felling necessitated for construction of highway and public projects in the state.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the Punjab and Haryana HC has imposed a blanket bank on tree felling without the HC’s prior permission which had brought to a standstill that strategic road projects in the border state even though necessary permission for these had been obtained from statutory authorities.The bench said the HC’s concern was legitimate as the forest cover in Punjab has been reduced to 3.67% of the geographical area, which is lesser than the 4.87% forest cover in the arid Rajasthan. Compensatory afforestation would be the best possible answer, the bench said.SG said that for that land must be made available by the state. The bench asked the state govt to file a detailed proposal on provisioning land for compensatory afforestation whenever trees are required to be felled for highway projects.The HC, while imposing a blanket ban on tree felling, had flagged the poor forest cover in the state and said, “It appears that the functionaries of the state of Punjab are neither serious nor they seem conscious of the impending ecological catastrophe.In view of the inactivity of the respondents, it requires drastic remedial measures by this court. Accordingly, this court prohibits the cutting of any tree of any age/species in Punjab, without permission of this Court, till the next date of hearing. ”In another case, the HC had said trees would be permitted to be cut if the state makes available and allots public land for the purpose of compensatory afforestation (planting of five times the number of trees cut) within a radius of five km of the place where the trees are felled. It had said that if the state failed to provide such land, then the cutting of trees would not take place.Mehta said that in linear highway projects, there may not be suitable land within five km of the project for afforestation and requested the court to relax this norm to enable afforestation at the nearest possible location.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asks Punjab govt its plan on allocation of land for compensatory afforestation in lieu of tree felling. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the Punjab and Haryana HC has imposed a blanket bank on tree felled.

NEW DELHI: Air India , Akasa Air and IndiGo have temporarily suspended or curtailed flights to Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh, following reports of explosions, including a loud blast at the city’s international airport, on Thursday.Akasa Air suspended flights to and from Riyadh through Saturday, while IndiGo cancelled its Riyadh services through Friday.Air India said a flight from Delhi to Riyadh returned to Delhi on Thursday and was subsequently cancelled “in the interest of safety”. The airline also suspended all flights to and from Riyadh until Saturday.Lufthansa Group, the German aviation company that owns Lufthansa Airlines and other European carriers, said its airlines would suspend flights to Riyadh through October 16 “due to current developments in the Middle East.”Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has claimed responsibility for the latest attack on Riyadh’s airport, saying a ballistic missile had caused damage, but provided no evidence. Saudi authorities did not immediately comment on the claim. The group’s military spokesperson later said the Houthis had fired additional ballistic and cruise missiles at airports in Riyadh and the southwestern city of Najran, claiming the strikes had disrupted flights.Riyadh’s airport had “closed again”, global flight-tracking service Flightradar24 said on X on Thursday afternoon. It reported that the last landing had taken place more than 80 minutes earlier and the last takeoff more than 90 minutes earlier.The developments came amid heightened safety concerns following a series of Houthi attacks on Saudi airports on October 6 and 7. Saudi authorities, as cited by the BBC, said a separate attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had killed one person and injured eight others. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted Saudi airports using ballistic missiles and drones.India on Thursday condemned the attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure “completely unacceptable”.“India condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries,” the Ministry of External Affairs said.“We express our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their loved ones. We wish speedy recovery for those injured. We express solidarity and stand with the people and government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” it added.

Article Title: Supreme Court: For post-split suicide, can't always accuse ex of abetment
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has held that when the break-up of a relationship ends in suicide, it cannot always be termed abetment and a former partner prosecuted.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran quashed criminal proceedings against a man and five of his family members who were being prosecuted for abetment after his live-in partner died by suicide after they broke up."People react differently to situations and if a breakup ends up with suicide, it cannot always be termed an abetment to suicide. The refusal to marry was not with an intention to drive the woman to death by suicide nor can knowledge be attributed to the accused that on such refusal, she would die by suicide," the bench said.The couple had been living together for a few mo-nths before the relationship ended. The woman's relative lodged a case against the man and five of his family members, including his parents."We are unable to find any instigation by the accused/appellants to drive the deceased to death by suicide. It was neither intended nor can it be said to be abetment. At worst, even if we fully believe what has been stated by the first informant, there was a refusal of marriage, which led to the woman committing suicide," it noted.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran quashed criminal proceedings against a man and five of his family members. The man's live-in partner died by suicide after they broke up. The couple had been living together for a few mo-nths before the relationship ended.

Article Title: 'Workers with AI skills in demand, but GenAI is hitting white-collar hiring'
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Generative AI has begun cutting into entry-level white-collar hiring in India even as the demand for wo-rkers with AI skills grows, signalling a labour market where some junior roles may disa-ppear while new occupations emerge, World Bank has said.In 'The World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence', it said GenAI reduced monthly job postings in India for white-collar occupations most amenable to AI and least complementary to it, with entry-level workers disproportionately affected.Across South Asia, job postings by firms declined 1.6% after ChatGPT's launch in Nov 2022, with a larger impact on multinational affiliates and suppliers linked to global value chains. Among the most exposed white-collar occupations where AI offers ready substitutes, monthly job listings fell by about 20%.Gaurav Nayyar, who led the World Bank team, told TOI the impact would not be uniformly negative. Some occupations in IT and knowledge-intensive services can be automated, he said, while other entry-level jobs would continue to grow and be complemented by AI. Roles like pro-mpt engineers and AI ethics specialists are also emerging.The "critical" part, Nayyar said, was for Indian IT businesses and higher education institutions to impart skills that allow workers to "pivot and adapt" as demands change. He cautioned against excessive specialisation, noting that coding, once seen as a lucrative standalone skill, became one of AI's early automation use cases. He argued for broad-based STEM education, engineering and scientific capacity that lets workers move across occupations.In the first half of 2025, AI-skill vacancies were over five times more common in high-income economies than middle-income ones, but India was among the leading middle-income countries.
Article Summary: GenAI reduced monthly job postings in India for white-collar occupations most amenable to AI and least complementary to it. Across South Asia, job postings by firms declined 1.6% after ChatGPT's launch in Nov 2022. Gaurav Nayyar, who led the World Bank team, said impact would not be uniformly negative.
